This update brings [b]new units, mission improvements, and performance improvements[/b] to the base game and both DLCs.[/p][p]Note that all Territory Mode content has been disabled in this beta update, but expect another major update for this upcoming new game mode soon. Please see the bottom of this post if you want to access the old Territory Mode beta on a separate Steam branch.[/p][p][/p][h3]Base game: New units & improvements[/h3][p]The Kwalasha campaign adds new units with unique roles. The [b]M4A Grinder[/b] is a light weapons platform capable of delivering rapid fire. Two new bipeds - the [b]M9A Sledgehammer,[/b] which carries a heavy mortar for long-range support, and the [b]M6A Jaeger[/b] with its heavy anti-armor gun and spotter drone - provide new mobile firepower. The [b]Hunter-Killer Merc[/b] is quite the opposite: delivering precise long-range strikes, aided by a companion drone for spotting and close support. Lastly, the [b]Merc Squad[/b] has also been upgraded with varied weapons for greater adaptability.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/c5f5156ac6b8d5f860d68e6518a9cf4695ddc379.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Urban Onslaught DLC: Improvements[/h3][p]Missions have been updated to feature the new units and the [b]A-12 Pegasus gunship[/b] can now unleash relentless rocket barrages on designated areas on the ground.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/4cbdf831d2df3e08aac0cbb44823f44a3d98ab00.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Many missions have been rebalanced or updated, integrating these new units in their respective campaigns. However, this is still in Beta, and we are working on more improvements.[/p][p][/p][h3]Note to our Map Makers[/h3][p]This update includes [b]significant balance changes[/b]! If you're creating or maintaining custom maps, be sure to [b]playtest your maps [/b]to ensure everything still plays as intended. [/p][p]We’ve also added a few new decorations—and we can’t wait to see how you’ll use them in your creative community maps![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/40b53a6d2e028de407ff5a35e4e06cccfd9dcdc9.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]How to join the Beta:[/h3][p][b]To participate in the beta program, go through the following steps:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Right click on Starship Troopers: Terran Command in your Steam Library[/p][/*][*][p]Click on Properties[/p][/*][*][p]Click on Betas[/p][/*][*][p]Click on drop-down menu and select "Beta - Open Beta"[/p][/*][*][p]Then Steam should automatically update the game and download the beta[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Old Territory Mode Beta[/h3][p][b]To access the old Territory Mode beta, go through the following steps:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Right click on Starship Troopers: Terran Command in your Steam Library[/p][/*][*][p]Click on Properties[/p][/*][*][p]Click on Betas[/p][/*][*][p]Click on drop-down menu and select "beta-territory-4.1.1 - Territory Mode Old Beta"[/p][/*][*][p]Then Steam should automatically update the game and download the beta[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]We hope you will enjoy the new content and that you will use the new units to tear those Arachnids a new one!  Be sure to join our [u][url="https://discord.gg/pcVuZ8njeA"]Discord server[/url][/u] to report any bugs or issues that you encounter in this beta. [/p][p]

notes.title: New Roadmap - 3rd Anniversary Update
notes.content:
[p]Troopers![/p][p]Next week, the 16h of June, is the third anniversary of Starship Troopers: Terran Command. To celebrate this - and to show you how we remain dedicated to supporting and expanding upon the game - we are sharing [b]the year 4 roadmap[/b] today.[/p][p]Without further ado, check the infographic below! But don’t stop there, as we go into more detail about its content further down in this post.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/6f88c3f2e1abd429b30349d1918a98ddda81013e.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Campaign Update | Summer 2025[/h3][p]The first free update brings [b]new content and improvements[/b] to the base game and both of the existing DLCs. [b]New player units[/b] have been added to the [b]Kwalasha campaign[/b] - and several are also available in the [b]DLC campaigns[/b]. Many Kwalasha missions have also been updated to focus on these new units and to enhance the overall experience.[/p][p]The [b]Raising Hell[/b] DLC will also receive a small amount of [b]new Mercenary unit types[/b], along with significant improvements to its campaign missions. The [b]Urban Onslaught[/b] campaign has additionally been [b]updated with several changes[/b] to its missions, mostly focused on the new units.[/p][p]In addition to all of the above, this update includes [b]significant performance improvements[/b], specifically targeting the slowdowns you may have experienced during long play sessions and on larger maps.[/p][p]All this new content will be available in the [b]Open Beta next month[/b].[/p][p][/p][h3]Territory Mode | Autumn 2025[/h3][p]If you’ve been following our Dev Diaries, you know we have [b]a new game mode[/b] - Territory Mode - in development. It offers unprecedented [b]freedom in unit selection and tactics[/b]. Played on new maps crafted specifically for Territory Mode, you’ll battle the Arachnids to [b]capture Territory Points[/b], adding a fresh strategic layer to the game.[/p][p]The base game and each DLC will get [b]exclusive Territory Mode maps[/b] and their own [b]unique Battle Group[/b]. Please see [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1202130/view/519714314320348464"]our last Dev Diary[/url] for full details, but in short: a Battle Group comprises a tailored [b]set of unit types[/b], [b]technologies[/b] and [b]gameplay mechanics[/b] - several available only to that group.[/p][p]Choose your Battle Group and challenge the Arachnids across countless [b]generated mission variations[/b]![/p][p][/p][h3]First “Battle Group” DLC | End of 2025[/h3][p]At the end of the year, we’ll release[b] a new type of DLC[/b] that is [b]focused exclusively on Territory Mode[/b]. Instead, you’ll gain exclusive access to a [b]uniquely themed Battle Group[/b] featuring its [b]own units, technologies and gameplay mechanics.[/b][/p][p][/p][h3]New “Story Campaign” DLC | Early 2026[/h3][p]Early next year another big “story campaign” DLC will drop. [/p][p]We hope you’re as excited as we are, Troopers - your war against the Bugs is only just getting started![/p][p]Service guarantees citizenship.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1202130/Starship_Troopers_Terran_Command/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #5: Territory Mode Battle Groups
notes.content:
Troopers! It’s about time for a big intel drop on the upcoming Territory Mode.

A lot of work is going into the new game mode behind the screens. In today’s Dev Diary we will delve deeper into the concept of Battle Groups, and how these form the core of the Territory Mode experience.

[h3]New modes, new menus[/h3]
The introduction of the new game mode has necessitated a redesign of the main menu. We’ve already highlighted this in a previous Dev Diary, but further changes have been made based on player feedback and new design requirements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/46241fa35c699fb6608dc1928a3c354ce859c6d5.png[/img]

When clicking the “GO TO WAR!” button, a new screen will require you to select a game mode: Story campaigns, challenge missions or Territory Mode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/4cb6f4f2cebc278f3d692550e0f8fe95db4b2bbd.png[/img]

[h3]Battle Group selection[/h3]
After entering Territory Mode, next you’ll be presented with the Battle Group selection screen. The base game and each DLC will come with its own Battle Group - each featuring a unique theme and set of exclusive units, mechanics and technologies. In this screen, you can also access a summarized information overview for each of the available Battle Groups.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/034c125c2e0b5bf7c5dc62af3540d3b0bd756fb9.png[/img]

[h3]Battle Group missions & progression[/h3]
Choose your Battle Group and you’ll enter the “Mission Selection Screen”. In this screen, missions will be available for you to accept on Kwalasha - the base game’s planet - or any of the planets from the DLCs that you own. This means that, regardless of which Battle Group you have selected, you can fight in any environment and against all Arachnid unit types that the game and DLCs offer. As we continue to release new DLC, this variety will only expand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/3bb11f8af0a53c14cd3272f19d5f4296e19457a9.png[/img]

Missions not only vary by planet, but also by starting tier, map type, objectives and Arachnid threats you’re expected to encounter.

The first time you start playing with a Battle Group, only a limited set of basic units and technologies will be available during the early missions. As you complete missions, however, you will unlock new unit types, new technologies and more complex, higher tier missions will become available. But beware, new Arachnid types and threats will also activate as you progress with the selected Battle Group.

Once you launch the selected mission, you’ll be taken into battle.

[h3]Playing a Mission[/h3]
A quick summary about Territory Mode gameplay: you capture territory points to acquire resources over time. These can be used to deploy units, call for reinforcements and to acquire new technologies. Technologies provide access to new unit types or apply upgrades that expand the performance or abilities of your units. For more information, see our previously released Dev Diaries.

Each Battle Group has its own set of technologies and unit types. Some of these may be shared with other Battle Groups, but many are exclusive and thus offer unique challenges and gameplay experiences.

The following screenshots show the different content available to the “Ground Pounders” - available as part of the base game - and the “Hellraisers” - available with the Raising Hell DLC. Note that this content is still in development and may differ once the Territory Mode is officially released.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/84d160e423553d6e43d7c9ec891ecc6323591b0c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/13f99f4b7eee3e280f42cc092295c3da5b94d8a8.png[/img]

The Technologies available during your mission depend on the mission's maximum Battle Tier, and is restricted to the content you have unlocked in the “Mission Selection Screen”.

If you manage to achieve all primary objectives - or fail a critical objective - the mission will end and you'll be taken back to the Mission Selection Screen. If a victory was achieved, new content may unlock. But regardless of the outcome, new generated missions will become available to choose - so you’ll always have new challenges ready to accept.

That’s all for now on Territory Mode, Trooper. For a final bit of news: Next month we’ll be announcing a new roadmap update - including still unannounced DLC content!

notes.title: Territory Mode - Dev Diary #4
notes.content:
Troopers! 

A lot of work is happening behind the scenes to bring major improvements to the upcoming Territory Mode. Today, we’re excited to share a few new teasers with you!

[h3]Territory Mode Progression[/h3]
We're currently focused on refining Territory Mode to enhance gameplay depth and variety. Our key priorities include:
[list][*] Improved onboarding – Ensuring that mechanics, units, and challenges unique to the new mode are introduced more gradually and intuitively.
[*] Greater mission variety – Developing a system that supports diverse objectives and dynamic narrative events for a more varied experience.
[*] New Territory Mode maps – The base game and all DLCs will receive their own sets of new maps specifically crafted for the new mode, greatly expanding their value and replayability.[/list]
[h3]New Raising Hell maps[/h3]
We are currently using the Raising Hell DLC as an example case for these Territory Mode refinements. The screenshots below show a few of the new Territory Mode maps we are adding to this DLC. Each map has been carefully designed to challenge your strategic skills and keep you on your toes against the Arachnid threat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/7cdd997ad73cf56f7b63b93584b9c1d997f43c82.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/66098aad967cb6f7856cb49074309192e42b5884.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/8aa60e3914a4cd532ff6cdbbdf48ad11fdadc589.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/c284a3037a3272d024cbcd91dcc5f6ddd88618e8.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/850a25f217d227180c8f952681e0e1bddc6ace48.jpg[/img]
[h3]Chariots Constructing Nests[/h3]
To wrap up this Dev Diary, here’s a sneak peek at one of the Arachnids' new abilities in Territory Mode: 

Chariot Bugs can now spawn from hives and move across the map to build static defenses. After claiming territory, they can construct structures such as Drone Nests, Hornet Nests, and Stinger Lairs. Tread carefully and always watch your perimeter—a small group of unassuming Chariots, left unchecked, can quickly erupt into a swarm of much more dangerous Arachnids!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/672ac99da4e0a820a90c0e45ac628158f7f16678.gif[/img]

Stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Territory Mode - Dev Diary #3
notes.content:
Welcome back, Troopers!

It has been two months since we rolled out the Open Beta for Territory Mode, and over [b]10,000[/b] of you have already joined the fight. We want to send a big thank-you to everyone who’s been battling the Arachnids and sending us invaluable feedback. Your reports from the frontlines continue to shape and improve Territory Mode.

We’re now focusing on [b]making the mode easier to learn, refining difficulty,[/b] and [b]adding more content[/b]. Meanwhile, we’re also working behind the scenes on our [b]next DLC[/b] - but that’s a story for another day.

[h3]A Note from the Engineering Corps: Savegames[/h3]
We’ve heard your requests, and our engineers have been hard at work behind the scenes to add [b]savegame support for Territory Mode[/b]. This upgrade means you’ll be able to save your progress and pick up right where you left off - no more losing hours of hard-fought territory gains because a sneaky Tanker decided to pop out of nowhere! We know you’ll appreciate fewer “rough moments” on the road to crushing the Arachnids.

[h3]Turret Troubles and Triumphs[/h3]
One of the recent changes in Territory Mode is how [b]turrets[/b] now behave when destroyed by Bugs. Rather than exploding into a pile of scrap, they enter a [b]“disabled mode”[/b]. Technicians, Engineers - or the fancy new repair drones, see below - can bring them back online, preserving any precious upgrades you invested in. Additionally, our artist is hard at work on [b]improved visuals for these disabled turrets[/b]. You’ll be able to tell at a glance which turrets can be repaired and returned to combat readiness, making it easier than ever to rebuild your defensive line after a crushing Arachnid assault.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/bef035134fcc9eb8deafe1723108ab08f129d270.gif[/img]

[h3]New Turret upgrade: Repair Drone[/h3]
In tandem with the turret visual improvements comes the [b]Repair Drone[/b] - a nifty upgrade you can requisition for your [b]Mortar Turret[/b]. Once unlocked, this flying friend will buzz around a radius, actively patching up damaged turrets. It’s the perfect backup when the frontlines are swarming and your Combat Engineers are busy clearing out Bug hives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/326c1ccd72dd35f136b902919073635445e6a970.gif[/img]

[h3]More to Come[/h3]
We’ve been flooded (in a good way!) with feedback and player data from your two months in the field, and there’s still more on the horizon. We can’t wait to share future updates, balance tweaks, and brand-new surprises as Territory Mode continues to evolve. [b]Keep those reports coming, Troopers[/b].

Haven’t joined the Open Beta yet? Suit up and help us refine Territory Mode into the best experience it can be. With every Bug squashed, every turret repaired, and every feedback form submitted, you’re helping the Federation stay one step ahead of the Arachnid threat.

Service guarantees citizenship. Now, get back out there and do your part!

[h3]Join the Open Beta[/h3]
You can access all this new content by joining the Open Beta through the following steps:
[list][*] Right click on “Starship Troopers: Terran Command” in your Steam Library
[*] Click on Properties
[*] Click on Betas
[*] Click on drop-down menu and select "Beta - Open Beta"
[*] Steam should now automatically update the game
[*] Launch the game to play the Open Beta version[/list]

notes.title: Territory Mode Beta - Major Update
notes.content:
Troopers, Assemble!

Today, as part of the RTS-Fest celebration, we have released a major update for the Territory Mode Open Beta. This includes balance changes, new features, new gameplay mechanics and new Territory Maps. 

[h3]Open Beta Update[/h3]

The Open Beta has been live for three weeks, and we’ve received invaluable feedback—thank you to all participants!
A detailed roadmap is coming soon, but for now, expect monthly updates with more maps, technologies, battle groups, and gameplay improvements. Your feedback is essential as we refine gameplay, balance, and technical stability. Keep it coming!
For those who need a quick recap: Territory Mode is a new game mode specifically designed for replayability. You fight the Arachnids over Territory Points on maps specifically crafted for Territory Mode. These points reward the player with the necessary resources required to purchase units, replace casualties and invest in new technologies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/95d9324fbca2bf6f2d20f9de411868520fe5fa25.png[/img]

[h3]Main menu update[/h3]

To support and present the new Territory Mode and all of its content, the main menu has been updated with a new content overview menu. This screen provides easy access to all content - Campaigns, Territory Mode and Challenge Missions - from the base game and the current and future DLCs.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/be0bec55293d2be0a11b1bf55e76e8a9c9f7ffd4.png[/img]
[h3]New Territory Maps[/h3]

Today’s update adds three new Territory Maps, doubling the amount that was previously available. This new set includes the first two maps that are exclusive to DLC owners.
[list]
[*] [b]Runway Rage[/b]: The Arachnids have overrun this air base, leaving many TAC Fighters stranded on the runway. This map is available for free as part of the base game.
[*] [b]Hotbed[/b]: We’ve established your base on top of a volcano to show the Bugs that we are not afraid! This map requires the [i]Raising Hell DLC[/i].
[*] [b]Party Crash[/b]: Evict the Bugs from the narrow streets, rooftops and metro stations of Mahanagar's nightlife district. This map requires the [i]Urban Onslaught DLC[/i].
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/b17a1ac9d4b67e579acc7cbd25024f0e257f488c.png[/img]

[h3]Join the Open Beta[/h3]
You can access all this new content by joining the Open Beta through the following steps:
[list]
[*] Right click on “Starship Troopers: Terran Command” in your Steam Library
[*] Click on Properties
[*] Click on Betas
[*] Click on drop-down menu and select "Beta - Open Beta"
[*] Steam should now automatically update the game

notes.title: Territory Mode - Dev Diary #2
notes.content:
Welcome back, Troopers!

We’re excited to share some more insights on [b]Territory Mode[/b], the new game mode that will be released as part of a free update, [b]next year[/b].

Want to jump in early and help us develop this new game mode? Then [b]sign up for the closed beta[/b] here!

https://www.slitherine.com/beta/starship-troopers-terran-command

[h3]A short recap:[/h3]
Territory Mode is a new game mode specifically designed for [b]replayability[/b]. A range of new maps has been created specifically for Territory Mode. In these maps, you can choose which units to use from the base game and from all DLCs that you own. For example, you can play with the Raising Hell DLC mercenaries against the new Bugs from the Urban Onslaught DLC.
In this game mode, Federation and Arachnid forces battle it out over Resource Points. These points reward the player with the necessary resources required to purchase units, replace casualties and invest in new [b]technologies[/b].
Now, let’s dive into another topic: the new and improved [b]Arachnid AI[/b], designed to test your tactical skills as you fight for every inch of territory.

[h3]Defenses and expansions[/h3]
When you start a new Territory Mode map, it will be crawling with Arachnids that won’t surrender their territory without a fight. While you expand your territory, the Bugs will try to retake it from nearby areas. If your defenses are poorly placed, the Bugs will outflank you and pierce through your territory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/2c675585005d38c7c9a03d507294873538b89697.gif[/img]

The more territory points you capture, the more paths the Bugs have to attack your territory. To hold the Arachnids at bay, you can rely on the multiple turret types provided by the Federation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/1c0d42a3bd3971345f19e9b10a226d0cb9b3cf57.gif[/img]

To keep the endless flow of Arachnid attacks on your territory running, the Bugs constantly reinforce their own territory from hives. Fed Intel has confirmed that clearing out all the hives in an area will neutralize the Arachnid threat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/910bf937cb3f084a7bb4fb8d30be37caa48dd03f.gif[/img]

[h3]Arachnid World Events[/h3]
While the Arachnids often rely on overwhelming the MI in head-to-head combat, they do have other tricks up their sleeves. (do Bugs have sleeves?)
A new tactic they have: While the MI is hard at work on the frontline, pushing forward and claiming territory, the Bugs will sneakily burrow through the ground to attack your back line. Make sure to keep some back up defenses and turrets in your territory!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/51d29b02b23734ce327f5cd56201dfb8b4fbb211.gif[/img]

This is only one of the many new fighting styles the Bugs have. Which events you will encounter will differ every time you start a new territory map, so you’ll have to decide which units and technologies to invest in. This offers [b]a different challenge each time you play[/b].
That’s all for this update. We can't wait to see how you will counter these new Arachnid threats. Stay tuned in the coming weeks for more information!

We have the ships. We have the weapons. We need soldiers. Soldiers like you! Do you want to do your part? Then [b]sign up for the closed beta[/b] here and help us improve this new game mode.

Troopers! Stand by for a briefing about the upcoming Territory Mode!

This brand new game mode will be released [b]early next year[/b] as part of a major free update, adding a ton of new content to both the base game and the two currently released DLCs. It is specifically designed to focus on player choices, customization and replayability. [h3]New maps & Territory Points[/h3]

Territory Mode is played on completely new maps, specifically crafted for the new mode. They often provide random starting bases and have unique layouts to offer a lot of [b]variation and different play experiences.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/f0820088527193e1d69cd404f7ca4cf2f5eccb26.png[/img]

The new [b]core feature of these maps are the “Territory Points”[/b], which are spread out across the playable area. Capturing these points will increase the amount of resources you gain over time (income).

[h3]Resource management & Technologies[/h3]

Territory Mode revolves around [b]a new resource type[/b]. This resource is required to purchase new units, to reinforce squads that have taken casualties and to [b]unlock technologies[/b]. These technologies will provide access to new unit types; and upgrades that expand the performance or abilities of your units. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/cb5bb76e6a1bbd75837bd1cfa75f8876c4c6fe30.png[/img]
Unlike Supplies and War Support, the new resource will not be refunded when you take casualties.
[b]Careful consideration of what to spend it[/b] on is vital to defeat the Arachnid threat.

[h3]Advanced Arachnid AI[/h3]

The Arachnids will not surrender their territory without a fight, and Federal scientists have found that [b]the enemy has become a lot smarter[/b]: Their strength will grow over time, they will reclaim lost territory points, form powerful attack waves and outflank your defenses. A mix of units and constructable turrets must be deployed to expand and to hold your territory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/bbbc2dad8b472ef2b94a90677d6c7762f9cabf00.png[/img]

In each Territory Mode game you may face a different set of [b]Arachnids threats, offering a wide variety of challenges[/b]. The right strategic choices of what units and technologies to employ will ensure that human civilization, not Bug insect, rules the galaxy now and always!

notes.title: DLC sneak peek: Turret defenses
notes.content:
[b]Greetings, Troopers,[/b]

In this update, we’ll provide a quick overview of the new turrets available in the upcoming Urban Onslaught DLC, along with a new resource type for acquiring these new units. Also, Closed Beta signups for the Urban Onslaught DLC are still open, if you are interested in giving feedback on the upcoming DLC you can still sign up!

[u][url=https://www.slitherine.com/beta/starship-troopers-terran-command-urban-onslaught]JOIN THE BETA HERE[/url][/u]

The Federation has provided access to a new line of advanced defensive turrets due to the increased Arachnid threat facing the great city of Mahanagar. Because each turret type has its own strengths and weaknesses, it is crucial to find the right mix and position them correctly to repel the Bug attack waves.

[h3]Autocannon & Mortar Turrets[/h3]
The Autocannon Turret is designed for engaging medium-armored and airborne enemies. It has good armor and high hitpoints, providing an excellent frontline barrier. But keep in mind that while this turret can fire over infantry units and most other turrets, it cannot fire over elevations or tall obstacles. Also, its efficiency decreases when engaging numerous targets due to the cannons overheating fairly quickly.
The Mortar Turret is designed to complement the Autocannon Turret, as it excels against masses of unarmored enemies with its large area of effect. It has indirect fire, allowing it to lob projectiles over both units and terrain elevations. However, the Mortar Turret projectiles are slow-moving, and the turret has a significant minimum range, making it ineffective against fast-moving targets and more vulnerable to direct attacks. 
Together, these two turret types provide a balanced defense against a wide range of lower tier Bug types.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/b7f3b489d38eb814196de16a30a8c203fffe5dcc.gif[/img]

[h3]Heavy Gun Turret & Sentry Turret[/h3]
The Heavy Gun Turret has a large cannon that fires projectiles capable of piercing even the most heavily armored Arachnids. The turret's drawbacks include a fairly slow reload time and slow rotation speed, which hinders its effectiveness against large numbers of enemies and fast moving targets.
The new Riot Shield Squad unit has the ability to launch a container that deploys a “Sentry Turret”. These small turrets operate autonomously and cannot be controlled directly by the player. They provide temporary, automated fire support, but expire after a short duration, making them ideal for creating brief strategic advantages during intense combat situations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/ae0be3fcc65e36cc9396a3c5d99c6750fb818015.gif[/img]

[h3]Ballistic Missile Turret[/h3]
Optimized for long-range engagements, the Ballistic Missile Turret boasts an impressive range and fires armor-piercing missiles. These missiles feature a built-in homing system that increases the likelihood of hitting moving targets. The turret is designed specifically for taking out hard-to-reach priority targets, as its very slow reload time makes it virtually useless in direct confrontations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/66287050460db89b850f711806ff3578e9300bc6.gif[/img]

[h3]New Resource: Materiel[/h3]
To acquire these advanced defensive units, a new resource type  has been introduced. This resource, called Materiel, is used for buying mechanical units and turrets. It regenerates slowly after losing units that require this resource, meaning frequent losses could cause significant delays in restocking and redeployment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/efe5b91d20a4550f9d4816a4e8e1f306db10d97a.gif[/img]

The Closed Beta for our Urban Onslaught DLC is still running. If you're eager to experience the new content first-hand and help shape its development, this is your chance! [url=https://www.slitherine.com/beta/starship-troopers-terran-command-urban-onslaught][u]Sign up for the closed beta here.[/u][/url]

That’s all for this update. We are certain that these new turrets will make you feel safer while defending your neighborhood. Lets just hope there is no Brain Bug present...

notes.title: Sneak Peek: Urban Onslaught DLC
notes.content:
[b] Attention, troopers, listen up! [/b]

Our team is hard at work crafting new missions, props, and units for the upcoming Urban Onslaught DLC. The initial missions are nearing a stage where we can start closed alpha testing. As we continue our efforts, we'd like to offer you a sneak peek at the new environments featured in the DLC, along with some visual improvements we are implementing.

[h2]New environments[/h2]

The upcoming “Urban Onslaught” DLC will introduce a range of exciting new environments. Set in a metropolis overrun by Arachnids, players can expect to explore various locations within the urban landscape. You will fight your way through towering skyscrapers, rooftops, construction sites, sewers, shopping streets, underground parking garages and more. Get set to defend the city and protect its civilians from the advancing Arachnid threat!

[previewyoutube=V9hzoPxdgbg;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Dropship visual refinements[/h2]

Refinements have been made to the visual presentation of dropships. Each dropship now has improved landing and take off animations with a more natural flight path. Furthermore, a new drop pod has been added to facilitate the deployment of larger units like the M11 Marauder or the upcoming Hover Autocannon unit. Larger squads, such as the Mobile Infantry, continue to be transported by the classic DR4-Viking, while smaller squads utilize the efficient DR8-Skyhook for deployment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/7e85790e4c2d64af6a34e691e0d972390a2200b2.gif[/img]

[h2]Turret pitching[/h2]

Among the improvements implemented in both the base game and DLC, turrets now have the ability to pitch up and down. It's a subtle change to the turret visuals that adds character and is used by several of the new units coming in the DLC. For example, the Hover Autocannon featured in the video below has a central turret platform designed to engage airborne threats effectively. A new set of defensive turrets will also be available in the DLC, which will be explored in an upcoming post.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/938d35e851be2bddafd443f5568e64c2a853e348.gif[/img]

[h2]Underground radio stations[/h2]

In this DLC, we're emphasizing expansive open maps, providing players with greater autonomy in choosing their own units. Given that several missions occur underground, we've introduced the ability to purchase units via underground radio stations. Moreover, players can now call in reinforcements from these stations, mirroring the mechanics of above ground scenarios.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/5751ba45d9d4077fbe75fb06b3770d38a56365a2.gif[/img]

We are starting closed alpha testing in the next few weeks. If you'd like to participate in alpha testing the new missions alongside developers in a live stream, you can sign up here:  https://www.slitherine.com/beta/starship-troopers-terran-command-urban-onslaught

notes.content:
Three new challenge missions for the Raising Hell DLC are currently in development. Owners of the DLC can already play them on the Open Beta branch. Scroll to the bottom of this post for more information on how to gain access.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2139990/Starship_Troopers_Terran_Command__Raising_Hell/

These missions give the player a lot of freedom in how to approach the objectives and which units to deploy. In addition, each mission has bonus objectives that increase your local high score.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/da63daa50db2d13be825d84eb5ca72a5b2aaf105.png[/img]

The main objective in this scenario is to gather soil samples at various locations by constructing and defending “prospectors”. In order to achieve this, you’ll have to muster a force of mercenaries in your outpost base and venture down into Bug territory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/7311703e4b51dd5053b153bddf4877aa3d0e926e.png[/img]

The scenario provides an excellent opportunity to experiment with various compositions of all the new mercenary unit types, both in an offensive and defensive role.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/af99218de55b21994fb2dd0ecdadede8a91c4764.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/6abbec6090ca3a2d76d4c566887b675129c9a674.png[/img]

While your starting base is important for the deployment of new units and infrastructure, the terrain offers various treacherous routes between Bug hives and additional Radio Stations. It is up to you to determine how to best approach the situation. 

The Federation cares for the wellbeing of its soldiers and their materiel. Your score will therefore be affected by the amount of losses taken. Careful positioning of your units and a correct response to new Arachnid threats will be vital to achieve a commendable outcome.

[b]Mission: Wildfire[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/968b72b5f5d5ce72beda55d16c2a70cd42a02391.png[/img]

This mission has a strong focus on the new Powered Suit Incinerators and Officer. Together with a flamethrower-equipped Marauder and various support units, they are tasked to exterminate a concentrated Bug infestation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/fb3d2e0f35098f59a91a49bcc47692400d442296.png[/img]

For an outstanding high score, all Nests need to be eradicated as quickly as possible, while additional points can be gained for clearing Bug Hives.

Attention, citizens of the Federation! Our mission to keep you informed continues as we explore the depths of the upcoming Raising Hell DLC, revealing new forces joining the battle for Gehenna. For protection of its people and assets, the corporation that exploits Gehenna for its valuable resources has relied on contracted mercenaries. notes.title: Breaking FedNet news - live from Gehenna
notes.content:
We now join our troopers live from the surface of what our brave colonists call “Gehenna”. It is here, on this unforgiving hellscape of molten lava and volcanic activity that the brave men and women of the Mobile Infantry beat back the Arachnid threat.

But why fight for this uninhabitable rock? Orbiting above lies the critically vital Vilon Station. A true feat of human ingenuity, the station provides the Federation with access to the vast fuel extraction and refining industry on the planet's surface. Thus, the station is a nexus of trade between Kwalasha, other Federation colonies and Earth.

Breaking News - The battle for surface is heating up, but worry not, as our reporter is embedded with the new and formidable “Engineering Biped”. As you can see, this machine was originally designed for heavy industrial labor, welding, drilling and the like. However, a combat redesign by security forces have turned this machine into an effective defense against the Arachnid aggressor.

It’s not just close quarters combat which is the Bipeds forte, as it possesses the elite ability to drop a trail of fire. Activating this ability gives the bipedal vehicle a speed boost, allowing it to quickly lay down a barrier of flames that can stop a Bug attack from reaching vulnerable positions.

[previewyoutube=RgrsXvnz0QA;full][/previewyoutube]

What is that? It appears to be one of the recently discovered Immolator Bugs! Scientists have yet to fully understand this endemic-to-Gehenna Arachnid, but comprehension of the enemy is not a requirement for its destruction! The heavy armor of the Engineering Biped is more than a match for this flame-spewing monster. But be careful troopers, this Bug has been known to make suicidal charges in its last desperate moments.

Scientists recommend that you keep your distance!

[previewyoutube=2Dm2LQTInA0;full][/previewyoutube]

Federal Engineering is truly something to behold, but don’t get complacent troopers. Disturbing reports of a new kind of flying bug have just recently arrived, and it’s a dangerous one. Nicknamed the “Bomberbee”, this ugly abomination carries a payload of deadly acid - released when it suicide bombs its victims.

Our mechanized units are particularly vulnerable, so be sure to shoot down these threats quickly troopers! 

[previewyoutube=2jTPm8-oiNQ;full][/previewyoutube]

That’s all from our live reporting for now, but if you would like to know more, why not volunteer to serve in the Mobile Infantry? Nobody knows when the next wave will be drafted, but some say it will most likely be in the fall. You’ll have your chance to experience this action and excitement for yourself.

Keep a keen eye out, and you too could be a Citizen.

notes.title: The free update Chemical Reaction is out now
notes.content:
[h3]Chemical Reaction Update[/h3]

After a period in Open Beta, we are releasing the Chemical Reaction Update for everyone.

Containing three new scenarios, one new unit type and the target priority setting, this is the largest free update so far.

[previewyoutube=tQwoYBw5S7c;full][/previewyoutube]

Let's have a look at its content:

- [b]Three new scenarios[/b], two of which make use of the first incarnation of a new high-score system;
- [b]One new unit type: Chemical Troopers[/b]; this unit is currently only available in the new scenarios, but there are plans to include it in future content as well. It's a squad of expert troopers using biochemical weapons, which they use to great effect for exterminating anything with more than two legs;
- [b]The Target Priority setting (TPS)[/b]; units can be set to prioritize firing at specific enemy types instead of aiming for the nearest target. For instance, if you want to automatically target Spitter Bugs with your Snipers, TPS allows you to avoid that level of micromanagement.

notes.title: Starship Trooper: Terran Command review: a slightly chaotic RTS that needs a bit more flavour
notes.content:
My biggest question about Starship Troopers Colon Terran Command was what tone it would strike. The RTS potential for an interplanetary ground war against overwhelming swarms of giant not-insects is obvious enough. But the dual spirit of most Paul Verhoeven films is a major reason that The Extraordinary Lust Of Dizzy (working title: Starship Troopers) still holds up 25 years on.

Terran Command understands that. Certainly it nods to the satire here and there, but mostly it focuses on the shooting and desperate defences and evacuations instead. This was the right decision. Though it's a little short on narrative flavour, unless you're really into exploring the setting, it's got enough tactical heft to make up for it.

notes.title: We tried the Starship Troopers strategy game, would you like to know more?
notes.content:
Steam's latest Next Fest has begun, and we're jumping in head first like we did last time by trying out a few demos to see what the future of strategy games has for us. Last time we brought you some early thoughts on Wartales, and now we're kicking things off with a brief look at Starship Troopers: Terran Command.

I'm a massive fan of the original '90s film (although the book was a bit highbrow for my sci-fi sensibilities), but even I recognise that its under-utilisation as an IP is mainly down to how unique that same film was. The bombastic score, the over-the-top characters and action, the fact that it didn't take itself too seriously... It's no wonder that subsequent attempts to bottle that magic have kind of fallen flat.

Enter Terran Command. It's the first Starship Troopers videogame since the 2012 mobile spin-off Starship Troopers: Invasion - Mobile Infantry, and before that there was the 2005 game simply called Starship Troopers. It's published by Slitherine and created by the same studio that brought you hardcore WWII war game Order of Battle. Let's set expectations early: based on the demo, this is easily the best Starship Troopers game ever, but that bar is pretty low, and this still may not tick all of the boxes.

notes.title: Upcoming tactical RTS Starship Troopers: Terran Command wants you to live forever
notes.content:
Starship Troopers is a strange license. The book is considered a classic in science-fiction literature, but the original film is the real gem and one of the finest things ever to have graced the earth. Don't at me.

Later films have been inconsistent, but there's not been much in the videogame world especially in the land of strategy games. The most notable release was Starship Troopers: Terran Ascendancy back in 2000. It was a tactical RTS game that was certainly fun, but a bit rough around the edges even by the standards of the time.

Towards the end of 2019 we were told that Slitherine are working on a Starship Troopers game of their own called Starship Troopers: Terran Command. It's another real-time tactical romp featuring a single-player campaign inspired by the original film spanning 21 missions. You will take part in the iconic attack on Klendathu, but spend most of your time on a new planet called Kwalasha created specifically for the game. You must take charge of the military forces on this vital outpost, and defend it from a growing Arachnid threat.

notes.title: Slitherine to debut new PC game "Starship Troopers - Terran Command" in 2020
notes.content:
Slitherine LTD, the world’s leading publisher of digital wargames and strategy games, in collaboration with Sony Pictures Consumer Products, announced today “[b]Starship Troopers - Terran Command[/b]”, a real time strategy game based on TriStar Pictures’s iconic 1997 movie to be released for PC in 2020.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pz_CKhycqN4

“[i]If you take one of the most iconic movies from the 90s and shape it into a strategy game of survival, that mixes classic real-time mechanics, tower defense and tactical deployment of units then you have ‘Starship Troopers - Terran Command’ in a nutshell[/i]”, says Iain McNeil, Development Director at Slitherine. [i]“Modern strategy games are fast-paced and they successfully blend unit management, survival and captivating storytelling. Nothing is more suited to this type of gameplay than the Starship Troopers universe, where there is a continuous sense of danger and uncertainty[/i]”.

Set in the same universe of the original movie, “Starship Troopers - Terran Command” drops players right at the heart of a human colony overrun by the Arachnids. They must take the fight into bug territory, where they will lead an army of elite soldiers to defeat the alien menace. They will deploy their units in strategic locations to cover vital choke-points, build defence emplacements, and achieve superior firepower through the tactical use of elevation levels.

“[i]When creating this game, we aimed to capture the essence of the original movie and its universe. This is not only achieved by creating a coherent set of units and scenarios, but also by mimicking the language, visual elements, dialogues and the little details that made the film such an iconic, cult feature[/i].”, Iain McNeil continues.

Slitherine is also a core strategy games publisher though and that doesn’t go away. This is why the British publisher is working with strategy games developer The Artistocrats to create a product that features complex mechanics, deep gameplay systems and a wide variety of options to turn a fast-paced strategy game into a mind-bending experience that involves multiple solutions to a very basic problem: to kill a lot of bugs.

The Artistocrats are the Belgian development studio behind the Order of Battle series and Commander: the Great War. Studio owner and lead designer Lukas Nijsten has been working on “Starship Troopers - Terran Command” for over two years now. The game is set to release in 2020.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v3Y5rJbktbM&feature=youtu.be

To find out more about “Starship Troopers - Terran Command,” check out the product page.
